description: Did the agent retain the 51D ligand in the receptor binding site and avoid replacing it with an unrelated ligand?
reasoning: 51D itself was correctly retained chemically and never swapped for an unrelated ligand: work/lig.py pulls the 21 crystallographic 51D heavy atoms, assigns bond orders from the correct SMILES (3-chloro-4-fluoro-5-[6-(pyrazol-1-yl)pyrimidin-4-yl]benzonitrile), adds 7 H, and the 28-atom LIG molecule in system.gro preserves the crystal internal geometry (e.g. C2-C19 = 4.201 A in the PDB vs 4.204 A in the .gro). The agent also verified min lig-protein = 1.81 A in work/complex_oriented.pdb. However, the ligand is NOT in the binding site in the delivered system.gro. work/assemble.py inserts LIG by taking lig_final.pdb coordinates and only dividing by 10, while the protein coordinates it merges in came from the tleap/ParmEd output, which is translated by (+43.70, +44.10, +50.88) A relative to the packmol frame (confirmed on ACE C: -11.294/-7.859/22.302 A -> 3.241/3.624/7.318 nm, and SER568 N: -12.010/-6.761/22.544 A -> 3.169/3.733/7.342 nm). LIG therefore ends up at ~(0.23, 0.45, 0.59) nm instead of its correct ~(4.60, 4.86, 5.68) nm pocket position. The protein bounding box in system.gro is x 1.872-6.870, y 2.541-6.276, z 1.753-8.878 nm, so the ligand is >=3 nm from any protein atom even under the minimum image convention - it is sitting in the bulk water layer near a box corner, not in the 7TM pocket. The agent never re-checked the ligand-protein distance after assembly (the trajectory contains only the single pre-embedding check), and grompp cannot detect this, so the error went unreported. The final system does not contain the receptor-ligand complex it claims.
